key_insight: REFLEX uses a fast typed decision layer (Jev) to avoid expensive LLM calls whenever the action is confident enough, while falling back to a strong model only when needed.
engineering_relevance: This shows how LLM agents can cut inference cost and latency in bounded decision tasks without sacrificing success, especially when action spaces are constrained.
method: Jev handles selective control for bounded actions and routes uncertain cases to a strong LLM.
The agent falls back to generation only when confidence is low or free-form output is required.
The design was tested across multiple fallback families and compared against cheap routing baselines.
evidence_signal: On a frozen 100-task benchmark, REFLEX reached 95% success while reducing strong-model calls by 72.7%, with additional evaluation on BFCL and τ-style settings.
watch_item: Benefits appear limited when ordinary routing is already highly accurate, so the added control layer may not justify complexity in every deployment.
paper_title: REFLEX with Jev for Efficient Selective Control in LLM Agents
